In response to Office No. 7482-GM/Aspar-MD dated July 6, 2011, I was instructed by the Commander of the Navy to transmit to you the following annexes, which consolidate the available records in the Brazilian Navy in the context of the Information Request No. 679/2011 from Federal Deputy CHICO ALENCAR:

a) An extract from the end-of-commission report of the Oceanographic Station: Ilha da Trindade, covering the period from November 1, 1957 to January 16, 1958, and prepared by Captain-ten-Commander CARLOS ALBERTO FERREIRA BACELLAR (Annex A);

b) Four photos obtained from photographer Mr. ALMIRO BARAÚNA on the occasion of the exhibition "Ilha da Trindade: the strength of the right - 100 years of Brazilian sovereignty" (Annex B); and

c) Four pages from "Substances for the Maritime History of Brazil - Chronicles of the year 1958" (Annex C).
Furthermore, I inform Your Excellency that there are no records in this Force that can provide answers to the raised questions.

On December 31st, a coded radio message was sent to EMA, informing DHN, that an unidentified flying object (UFO), in the shape of a flattened ellipsoid, colored stainless steel, at an altitude of approximately 1600 meters, was observed moving at a vertiginous speed in a northeasterly direction, without making any noise. The object was seen by Dr. 1st Lieutenant Ignácio Carlos Moreira Murta, 1st CI-SI Sebastião Soriano de Souza, and five workers from Companhia Moraes Rego, one of whom—the first to spot the object—stated that he had seen it previously on December 5th and had reported it to his colleagues, but it was not taken seriously. Both times, it was close to 8 a.m.

The following day, January 1° th, all attention was focused on the sky when something appeared, observed by around twenty men from the garrison, which was confirmed to be the same object; I was also alert and it seemed to me, however, to be a seagull. The object—or seagull—was flying directly overhead, making depth perception impossible; moving in a northeasterly direction, it suddenly shone intensely at some point in its trajectory, though perhaps for less than a second. If it was a seagull, its speed would have been considerable but within reason; if it was indeed the object, it should have been at a considerable distance, and in that case, its speed was incredible. This incident was not reported to EMA due to the lingering doubt.

Finally, on January 16th, around 1100, I was already on board the NE "Almirante Saldanha" after the change of command at the post, when I was notified that an unidentified aerial object had been seen from the ship over the island. I was in my cabin at the time and immediately went to the deck, where I found several people, including Mr. Almiro Baraúna, a professional photographer, who had accompanied several diving hunters to the island of Trindade to take underwater photographs. Mr. Baraúna was one of the most excited as he had taken several plates of the object and was eagerly awaiting positive results, doubting whether he had succeeded. I did not leave his side to verify the authenticity of the negatives. I saw him remove the film roll from the camera and went to the darkroom to watch the development, as it was too hot to enter, so I waited outside for the duration of the operation, about 10 minutes. Leaving the darkroom, still with the film in the basin, I saw him remove it and witnessed his disappointment as he, visibly nervous, assumed he had failed. I took the film, examined it more closely, and in three negatives from different positions, I noticed the presence of a strange stain that was later perfectly identified. The film remained in Mr. Baraúna's possession, who, upon my insistence, agreed to come to EMA if necessary. Upon my arrival in Rio, I went there and dealt with the case with CC José Geraldo Brandão, providing a verbal statement. From that point on, everything that was done was at the exclusive initiative of EMA.
Brasilia, October 2, 2011.

JOSÉ ROBERTO BUENO    JUNIOR

On the evening of __UFO_PROTECTED_000__, a peculiar phenomenon was observed in the sky over the small town of __UFO_PROTECTED_010__. Several residents reported seeing a bright, disk-shaped object moving erratically at high speed. The object appeared to be hovering for a moment before suddenly disappearing.

The local police received multiple calls from frightened citizens, all describing a similar object. Officer __UFO_PROTECTED_020__, who responded to the first call, reported that the object was "like nothing he had ever seen before." He described it as a flat, circular shape with bright lights surrounding it.

A local scientist, Dr. __UFO_PROTECTED_030__, was contacted by the police and asked to investigate the phenomenon. He arrived at the scene and conducted a thorough examination of the area, interviewing witnesses and collecting evidence. Dr. __UFO_PROTECTED_030__ concluded that the object was most likely a man-made device, possibly a experimental aircraft or a weather balloon, but he could not rule out the possibility of an extraterrestrial origin.

The incident gained widespread attention in the local media, sparking a flurry of speculation and debate. Some residents were convinced that it was a sign of extraterrestrial life, while others were skeptical and attributed the sightings to natural phenomena or human error.

Despite the conflicting opinions, the event left a lasting impression on the community. It became a part of local folklore, with stories of the mysterious object being passed down through generations. Even today, some elderly residents of __UFO_PROTECTED_010__ still speak of the night the sky was lit up by an unknown visitor from above.

February 21 — The press continues to deal with the photographs taken by a civilian photographer who, by invitation, was observing the work of the International Geophysical Year being carried out in the NE Saldanha da Gama.

Bulletin No. 8 of this year publishes Opinion No. 193 of June 12, 1957, from the Legal Advisory Council of the Navy, stating that there is nothing to prevent military personnel from being registered in the Order of Brazilian Lawyers; nor are they required to obtain authorization to do so.

By Notice No. 513, the NH Canopus is incorporated into the Navy's service.

February 22 — The press publishes the photographs obtained by the civil photographer who was on board the Gama, and controversies arise about their authenticity.

The Ministry of the Navy issues the following Official Note:

"Regarding the news disseminated by the press that the Minister of the Navy has opposed the dissemination of facts concerning the appearance of a strange object over the island of Trindade, this Office clarifies that such information lacks foundation.

This Ministry does not see reasons to prevent the publication of photographs of the aforementioned object, obtained by Mr. Almiro Baraúna, who was on the island of Trindade at the invitation of the Navy, in the presence of a large number of elements of the guard."

"2. Relatos de avistamentos de objetos voadores não identificados (OVNI) ou 'ufos' são registrados em todo o mundo desde o século 19. As observações variam de luzes brilhantes no céu a objetos em forma de disco ou de barco, muitas vezes relatadas como se movendo em velocidades incomuns ou exibindo manobras impossíveis para aeronaves convencionais.

Os casos mais famosos incluem o incidente de Roswell em 1947, onde um objeto supostamente de origem extraterrestre foi supostamente encontrado no Novo México, EUA; e o incidente de Phoenix em 1997, onde um objeto em forma de disco foi visto por centenas de pessoas em Arizona, EUA.

Embora existam muitas teorias sobre a natureza dos OVNIs, incluindo a possibilidade de tecnologia alienígena avançada, até o momento não há evidências conclusivas que comprovem a existência de vida extraterrestre ou a origem sobrenatural dos avistamentos."

segments.text: Greetings, I refer to Office No. 7483-GM/Aspar-MD dated July 6, 2011, regarding Unidentified Flying Objects (UFO) and the "Request for Information No. 679/2011" authored by Federal Deputy Francisco Rodrigues de Alencar Filho.

Regarding the matter, the Deputy requests additional information from this Force regarding the generation, possession, and provision of public documentation required by scholars of the phenomenon of unidentified flying objects.

3. Regarding the inquiries made to this Force and described in item 3. of the Information Request No. 679/2011, I have been instructed by the Commander of the Army to provide the following information:

missing_from_translation: Fátima da Silva e Valquíria Aparecida

segments.text:
a) Are the statements of the identified witnesses in the __JUSTIFICAÇÃO__ (Justification) of this Request, as "1st Military," "2° Military," and "3° Military," recorded and in the possession of several individuals who investigated the Varginha Case, known to the Ministry of Defense?

Although the question is directly addressed to the Ministry of Defense, they are merely other versions from unidentified individuals and, therefore, are not within the knowledge of the Brazilian Army, nor were they listed in the administrative procedures established at the time.

b) Why were the witnesses directly involved in the sightings and captures of the supposedly extraterrestrial creatures in Varginha, such as students Kátia Andra de Xavier, Fátima da Silva, and Valquíria Aparecida da Silva, and lower-ranking military personnel from the Military Fire Department (CBM) and the Military Police (PM) of Minas Gerais, not heard nor in the investigation nor in the Military Police Inquiry (IPM) 18/97 opened at the School of Sergeants of Arms (ESSA)?

The command of the Sergeant's School (ESSA) has initiated an investigation to clarify the alleged involvement of military personnel from the school, as reported in written, television, and radio media, in the region of the cities of Varginha - MG and Três Corações - MG. All military personnel "mentioned by the media" have been included in the investigation, and it has been determined that they did not participate in any cargo transport operation.

c) What are the actual versions of the Army for the witness "12   Military's" report,
especially regarding the timings and the morphological descriptions of the strange creatures seen
in Varginha, since, according to the IPM files (Fls. 219, 220, 261, 322, 323, 324, 325, 326, 327,
and 328) conducted for the purpose of conclusion, the being sighted in the afternoon of January 20,
1996 by the students - not heard in the said IPM - would have been a result of a mix-up with "Mr.
Mudinho", and not an "extraterrestrial being"?

The actual version of the Brazilian Army is what resulted from the administrative procedures established, in which there is no mention of the interrogation of a witness titled "1st Military" but rather individuals with their basic qualification data.

d) If the Army received the first creature from the CBM on the morning of January 20, 1996, as stated by the "1° Military", what was the final destination given to it, where are the documents or any other types and formats of data related to these information, and what is their current classification level of secrecy?

There was no receipt or embarkation of any type of military-use cargo, and the only documents produced by the Institution were the investigation and the Military Police Inquiry (IPM).

segments.text: (e) How and why the investigation initiated by the Commander of the ESSA, General Sérgio Pedro Coelho Lima, just six days after the press conference held at the lawyer Ubirajara Franco Rodrigues' home, aiming to "investigate facts regarding news published in the press about the involvement of military personnel from that School in the capture of the 'Varginha ET', presents as justification for the abnormal movement of Army trucks observed at the epicenter of the events during the weekend from January 20 (Saturday) to 22, 1996, two documents: one is an expenditure note 96NE00033 from the Integrated Federal Financial Administration System (SIAFI), dated January 23, 1996, in favor of the concessionaire, and the respective service invoice issued by the company on January 29, 1996 (Files 43 and 44 of the IPM)?

The documents cited contain the description of the vehicles dispatched to the city of Varginha to receive maintenance services at the concessionaire.
              (f) Even if the Army truck convoy went to Varginha for mechanical services days before they were performed at Automaco SA - which is not mentioned in the investigation statements - what were these vehicles doing in the Andere Garden, the neighborhood where the first creatures were reportedly spotted and captured, and at the Regional and Humanistic hospitals, where they were reportedly taken later, since these epicenters of the Varginha Case are kilometers (inland) away from the route linking Automaco concessionaire to ESSA in Três Corações/MG?

missing_from_translation: Casa Civil da Presidência da República

segments.text:
More than fifteen years after the supposedly occurred event, it becomes impossible to determine the reason for the displacement of those vehicles in the mentioned region.

g) Why did the Army not inform the existence of the IPM (Inter-Agency Panel on Unidentified Flying Objects) to the Ministry of Defense when it was officially requested by the Civil House of the Presidency of the Republic in 2008 to comment on the generation or possession of UFO documents by the Three Armed Forces, only providing a response in 2010 when this Chamber of Deputies requested it through RIC 4470/2009?
(from Office 0808-A/3.8, of August 4, 2011)

missing_from_translation: Requerimento da Comissão Brasileira de Ufólogos

segments.text: In the general protocol of the Office, no request regarding the subject was found for the year 2008. Only on January 21, 2010, was the first request made for the Army Command to comment on the Brazilian Commission of UFOlogists' request, and this Ministry was responded through the official document number 0170-A/3.2, dated March 11, 2010.

h) What was the reason for the alleged fear of the ESA Command, or the Army Intelligence, that prevented the clarification and disclosure to ufologists and the press in general of the internal inquiries conducted by that School between May 1996 and June 1997, and its conclusions that the "Varginha ET" was no more than "Sr. Mudinho"?

At no point did the Force omit or fail to clarify facts that were in the public domain. Allegations to the contrary are mere speculations.

(i) What reasons led to the "polite, friendly, and just" request for silence regarding 0 IPM, made by military personnel from ESSA to the researcher and lawyer of Vitório Pacaccini, Ubirajara Franco Rodrigues?

As described in the Information Request itself, the citation posted on the internet by Mr. Ubirajara Franco Rodrigues is a recent comment and, as such, was not the target of the investigations conducted during the administrative procedures established at that time.

(j) Having concluded the inquiry on May 21, 1996, without any military personnel from ESSA having been punished for committing any illicit act, why would the commander of that school initiate a new investigation procedure, this time an IPM (Internal Investigation Process), eight months later, with the aim of determining if the authors of the book "Incidents in Varginha - Creatures from Space in Southern Minas," Vitório Pacaccini and Max Portes, committed new illicit acts, when everything recorded in the book had already been reported by the press, ufologists, and investigated by the equally secretive previous ESSA inquiry?

The IPM, established on January 29, 1997, aimed to investigate the content
of the work titled "Incident in Varginha - Space Creatures in Southern Minas."

k) In addition to the discussed diligences that led to the investigation and IPM, the
Terrestrial Force conducted any other internal procedures or in conjunction with other
government institutions, such as the Fire Department or the Military Police of Minas Gerais,
using its logistics during the initial months of 1996 in Varginha and its surroundings,
resulting in the capture of strange creatures and/or the rescue of an unidentified object,
forwarding these things to other institutions like the Humanists Hospital and the University
of Campinas, storing them in military areas or transporting them to other agencies, as cited by
other civil witnesses in Pacaccine and Portes' work, but who were not heard during the ESSA's
inquiries?

No military installation or military equipment was used to store or transport any type
of cargo, as referenced in the Information Request No. 679, 2011. The genuine information and
investigations about the aforementioned events in the region of: Varginha - MG and Três
Corações - MG are contained in the administrative procedures established and properly
forwarded to the 4th Military Judicial Circuit, an organ of the Judiciary, who was responsible
for deciding on the matter.

Given this, the Commander-in-Chief of the Army has instructed me to emphasize that this
Force does not have any other materials or documents related to the subject, besides those sent
to the 42 Military Judicial Circuit.
Sincerely,
